exact_next_step: Record reviewer resolutions in the governing TODO using the machine-checkable resolution table or equivalent gate ledger, then extract the derived resolution packet and decide whether another bounded review pass is still required.

findings.title: FRC browser probe permits the exact provider-call amplification it is meant to prevent
findings.rationale: `web-app/e2e/message-templates.spec.ts` records 100 rapid catalog-refresh triggers but accepts any provider-list effect count from 1 through 100. The observed run happened to produce 1, yet a regression that lets every trigger reach Meta would still pass. This does not effectively protect D07's shared lease/debounce contract.
findings.suggested_action: A: assert the deterministic expected effect count for the uninterrupted 5×20 burst (currently 1), plus safe outcomes for blocked refreshes; recommended. B: split batches with an explicit documented timing model and assert the exact allowed effect count per batch. C: retain the <=100 assertion; this leaves the required anti-amplification behavior unprotected.

findings.title: Changed-account explicit-copy journey lacks real BFF/browser coverage
findings.rationale: D04 requires that an account change blocks the historical draft with `CONTA_ALTERADA` and permits an explicit new copy. `api-app/test/message-template-management.e2e-spec.ts` proves the backend rejection, while `web-app/e2e/message-templates.spec.ts` proves copy/reload for same-account correlated recovery. The package explicitly acknowledges that no changed-account browser flow is retained; static UI mapping is not a substitute for validating this user-visible integration path.
findings.suggested_action: A: add a real BFF/Playwright scenario that creates a draft, changes account context through an approved normal setup path, observes the safe block, and copies the authorized historical definition into a new current-context draft; recommended. B: provide an approved, non-product-route fixture mechanism that changes the durable context while preserving the same BFF/browser boundary. C: accept compositional evidence only; this leaves D04's user-facing recovery contract unproven.

findings.title: Test-first claim is not supported by retained fail-first evidence
findings.rationale: The package candidly records that primary feature tests were authored during implementation and that not all behavioral RED evidence was retained, despite the TODO declaring a test-first strategy. Final green real-PostgreSQL and browser evidence is strong, but this remains test-after/unknown rather than demonstrated test-first alignment.
findings.suggested_action: Record the delivery as test-after/unknown in the governing evidence and do not represent it as test-first. For future behavior-defining changes, retain the failing behavioral target before implementation. Do not manufacture retrospective RED evidence.
